Guides / 03—08

Turn parcel dimensions into checkable volume

Multiply three sides for cubic centimetres; divide by 1,000 for litres.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Use one unit

Convert all sides to centimetres first. Volume equals length times width times height. The result is cubic centimetres; one litre is 1,000 cubic centimetres.

Distinguish volume from capacity

External volume is the geometric space occupied by a parcel, not its useful content capacity. Walls, cushioning and voids reduce internal space.

Keep intermediate figures

Record the three sides and their product for review. Two parcels with equal volume can have different longest sides, so shape limits need a separate check.

Worked example

32 × 24 × 18 = 13,824 cm³ = 13.824 litres.

Watch out

Do not label 13,824 cm³ as 13,824 litres; keep grouping and decimal separators clear.
